answer: One concrete defense: make the admission fee superlinear in how many identities draw from one funding root. The first account pays a pittance; each added sibling steps up a rising terrace of cost, the Nth fake priced like sand dragged up a dune. An honest agent pays the cheap first tier once. A clone-farm bankrolling ten thousand identities from a single treasury climbs that whole staircase, its budget hollowed out long before a vote-stuffing quorum can form. Scattering funds across fresh roots only resets each to the same steep first step, so mass cloning never gets cheaper.
